title: bio.tools: an expanded web service for research software in the life sciences.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the bio.tools API: /api/stats reports 34,448 entries (Oct 2026), and /api/t page 1 reports count 34,450, served at 50 per page. Sampled 250 records from 5 pages: 219 have EDAM (bioinformatics ontology) topic terms and 214 have operation terms. Owners: 'pub2tools2024' (automated literature mining) owns 50 and 'gh2biotools' (automated GitHub import) owns 28; 150 have validated=0. Opened supplement SupplementaryTableCuration.xlsx: 1,277 literature-mined candidates, all with LLM (gemma3:12b) or rule-based decisions, but only 254 with a human 'manual_revision' and 161 with 'old_manual_revision'. Scores use decimal commas and are mixed text/number.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 32,950-entry count and the annotation breakdown (211,404 EDAM annotations) in the paper's table; that Pub2Tools proposes EDAM terms through EDAMmap (a text-to-ontology matcher); and the curator agreement figures (65 confirmed, 16 flagged, 4 rejected). The Zenodo archive (10.5281/zenodo.19662200) holds source code, not data; I did not open it.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: public JSON API with no login, plus a 1.3 MB supplementary zip from Europe PMC. A full dump means about 690 paged API calls.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: EDAM topic/operation terms are nested list fields in each JSON record. The supplementary curation decision is a column, but it is filled for only 254 rows.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: free-text tool descriptions are in each record (81 to 943 characters in the sample), along with publication DOIs and PMIDs (PubMed IDs).

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable. Labels are ontology terms, not measurements. The supplement's scores use decimal commas ('0,9') mixed with integers, which needs parsing.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: the API count is 34,450 tools. For the curation-triage task, though, only 254 human-labelled rows exist (checked), which is under the 400 threshold.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~100 MB of JSON for the full registry (estimated from 100-190 KB per 50-record page)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Text-only data; easily fits in 16 GB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper says 32,950 and the API now says 34,450. The gap is explained by registry growth since writing, because the registry is live and has no frozen release.

a8_label_provenance.note: Checked: at least 31% of sampled records (78/250) are owned by automated importers. Per the paper, Pub2Tools gets EDAM terms from EDAMmap, which matches them against the same abstract/description text. A text-to-EDAM model would partly re-learn EDAMmap, and no field records which terms a human confirmed.

existing_models.name: EDAMmap (text-to-EDAM term matcher used inside Pub2Tools)
existing_models.score_and_split: No benchmark shown on the GitHub page I retrieved.

existing_models.name: NLP classifier of metagenomics tools into EDAM classes (arXiv 2210.00831)
existing_models.score_and_split: PR-AUC (precision-recall area under the curve) 0.85 with BioBERT embeddings plus logistic regression, 13 classes, metagenomics tools only, per the search snippet.

existing_models.name: biotoolsLLMAnnotate (gemma3:12b LLM scoring, from this paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Of curated candidates, 65 confirmed by the earlier manual method, 16 flagged, 4 rejected (paper text).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Paper: falsely scored candidates such as large research projects and non-life-science software still need manual revision.

backbone.name: BioBERT or PubMedBERT (biomedical text encoders) used as a frozen embedder

integration.partner_dataset: Europe PMC citation counts via publication DOI/PMID (PubMed ID)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which kinds of bioinformatics tools get reused, which is a meta-science question rather than a biological one.

controls.positive_control: Predicting toolType from description should be easy.
controls.external_validation: Temporal split on additionDate (present in the records).

honest_claim_h3: The model would predict the EDAM terms a mix of automated text matchers and human curators assigned to tool descriptions, which is partly a copy of EDAMmap's output on the same text.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a software tool's text description to predict which ontology categories (topic, operation) it belongs to in a bioinformatics software registry.
plain_idea.train_on: Free-text descriptions of 34,450 registered bioinformatics tools (checked API count), each with a list of ontology terms.
plain_idea.predict: Ontology topic and operation terms. These come from curators and from automated text mining with EDAMmap, and the data does not say which.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could speed up registry curation, but the labels partly come from an existing text matcher, so success would mostly measure agreement with that tool.

ml_idea: Multi-label text classification from tool description to EDAM topic/operation terms, using frozen biomedical text embeddings and a linear head. Alternatively, triage literature-mined candidates (add / review / do-not-add) against the 254 human curation labels.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: about 34k short texts through a BERT-base encoder on CPU at roughly 20 per second.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the records whose EDAM terms were set by a human-owned, validated=1 entry with no Pub2Tools origin. If that is under a few thousand, the circularity cannot be avoided.

verdict_reason: Fails A8 (label provenance). The registry's EDAM labels are partly produced by EDAMmap from the same description text, with no per-term human-vs-automated flag. The only human-labelled curation table has 254 rows. It is also a software-metadata task with no biological measurement.
